title: The differentials of a p-independent family are linearly independent
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number and $K/k$ a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] of fields of characteristic $p$. Let $K^p=\{b^p:b\in K\}$ and let $kK^p$ be the subfield of $K$ generated by $k$ and $K^p$. Let $(x_i)_{i\in I}$ be a family of elements of $K$ which is $p$-independent over $k$, i.e. the monomials $x^E=\prod_{i\in I}x_i^{e_i}$, where $E=(e_i)_{i\in I}$ runs over the families of integers with $0\le e_i<p$ for all $i$ and $e_i=0$ for all but finitely many $i$, are linearly independent over $kK^p$ (as a family indexed by $E$). Let $\mathrm d:K\to\Omega_{K/k}$ be the module of Kähler differentials of $K$ over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Then the family $(\mathrm dx_i)_{i\in I}$ is linearly independent over $K$ in the $K$-vector space $\Omega_{K/k}$.

proof.text: (Extension to a $p$-basis.) By [lem-weil-pbc-p-independent-extends-to-p-basis] applied to the extension $K/k$ of fields of characteristic $p$ and the family $(x_i)_{i\in I}$, which is $p$-independent over $k$ by hypothesis, there are a set $J$ and a family $(y_j)_{j\in J}$ in $K$ such that the combined family $(z_l)_{l\in I\sqcup J}$ ($z_i=x_i$ for $i\in I$, $z_j=y_j$ for $j\in J$) is a $p$-basis of $K$ over $k$: the monomials $z^E=\prod_lz_l^{e_l}$, $E=(e_l)_{l\in I\sqcup J}$ with $0\le e_l<p$ and almost all $e_l=0$, form a basis of $K$ over $kK^p$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07P2 (lemma-p-basis), proof, third paragraph ('Any p-independent subset can be enlarged to a maximal one ... The claim will imply that (1) implies (2)')

proof.text: (The differentials of the $p$-basis form a basis.) The family $(z_l)_{l\in I\sqcup J}$ of Step 1 satisfies the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-p-basis-differentials-basis] for the extension $K/k$ (same $p$, same subfield $kK^p$, index set $I\sqcup J$). Hence $(\mathrm dz_l)_{l\in I\sqcup J}$ is a basis of the $K$-vector space $\Omega_{K/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07P2 (lemma-p-basis), proof, second paragraph ('(a) implies (b)'), applied as the third paragraph says

proof.text: (A subfamily of a basis is linearly independent.) Let $F\subseteq I$ be finite and $c_i\in K$ ($i\in F$) with $\sum_{i\in F}c_i\,\mathrm dx_i=0$ in $\Omega_{K/k}$. Since $\mathrm dx_i=\mathrm dz_i$ for $i\in I\subseteq I\sqcup J$, putting $c_l=0$ for $l\in(I\sqcup J)\setminus F$ gives $\sum_{l\in I\sqcup J}c_l\,\mathrm dz_l=0=\sum_l0\cdot\mathrm dz_l$, and uniqueness of the coordinates in the basis of Step 2 gives $c_l=0$ for all $l$, in particular $c_i=0$ for $i\in F$. So $(\mathrm dx_i)_{i\in I}$ is linearly independent over $K$ in $\Omega_{K/k}$.
